newsitem.title: USA: Tro Learning shares tumble after earnings report.
newsitem.headline: Tro Learning shares tumble after earnings report.

text.p: TRO Learning Inc. stock lost half its value Tuesday after the maker of educational computer software reported disappointing earnings and said the results caused it to violate the terms of a bank loan.
TRO stock tumbled $8.875 to $8.375 in active trading on Nasdaq, where it was the biggest loser of the session.

Based in suburban Hoffman Estates, Ill., TRO said late Monday it earned $2.3 million, or 34 cents a share, in its fourth quarter ended Oct. 31, down sharply from the $4.4 million, or 71 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter. Revenues were flat at $16.9 million.
Analysts had forecast earnings of $1.04 a share for the quarter, according to First Call, which tracks Wall Street earnings estimates.

"As a result of the earnings shortfall the company is in technical noncompliance with certain of the financial covenants of its loan agreement," Chairman William Roach said in a statement. "The company is seeking a waiver from its bank which it expects to receive."
The company said orders for its Plato Education software surged 56 percent in fiscal 1996 but that it could not recognise the orders as sales under accounting standards.

"The company had a strong 1996 in terms of orders for its Plato coursewear," said Alexander Paris Jr., an analyst at Barrington Research Associates Inc. "Management probably wanted to report the orders as income, while the accountants said (the company) couldn't."
The company's offices were closed Tuesday for the Christmas holiday.
TRO management several weeks ago announced a delay in announcing fourth-quarter results "and it was probably because of this issue," Paris added.
TRO develops computer-based interactive education software for schools, corporations and government.
